name: chipgen
summary: Generative chiptune on real YM2612 + SN76489 emulation, driven by a flat event vocabulary any model can emit.

YM2612.role: 4-operator FM; channel 6 doubles as an 8-bit PCM DAC

revisions.ym2612: discrete (Model 1 / Model 2 VA2) — has the DAC ladder, so muting bleeds and silence is gritty

inputs.tracker: compact text grid; see python/tracker.py docstring
inputs.json: array of event objects; see events

outputs.vgm: VGM 1.71 register log; plays in VGM players, imports into DefleMask and Furnace. .vgz gzips it.
outputs.tracker: the score written back out as text

bass.character: punchy FM bass, fast attack, short body

bell_pluck.character: bright metallic pluck/bell, good for arpeggios

brass.character: FM brass section, brightens after the attack

distorted_lead.character: gritty overdriven lead, heavy feedback, cuts through

e_piano.character: DX-style electric piano, bell-tinged, decays away

jazz_chord_pad.character: soft additive chord tone, one note per channel

organ.character: additive drawbar organ, sustains flat until note off

slap_bass.character: snappy funk bass with a bright attack transient

sub_bass.character: pure sine sub, no harmonics, sits under everything

Wait.doc: Advance the sequence clock by `ticks` ticks.

Tempo.doc:
Change how long a tick lasts, from this point on.

    Lets one event stream carry tempo changes without the caller having to
    re-time everything: a ritardando is a few Tempo events, not a rewrite.

LoopPoint.doc:
Mark where a VGM player should jump back to when the track ends.

    Ignored by the audio renderer (a WAV has no loop), consumed by vgm.py.

Marker.doc:
Free-text annotation: section names, comments, model reasoning.

    Renders to nothing. Useful for keeping a model's own structure notes
    inside the event stream instead of alongside it.

FMInstrumentSelect.doc: Assign a preset instrument (see instruments.BANK) to an FM channel (0-5).

FMPan.doc:
Stereo placement plus LFO sensitivity for one FM channel (register 0xB4).

    The chip pans per channel by hard-muting an output, not by a
    continuous law: left/right are on/off flags, and "centre" means both
    are on. ams/pms are how strongly the global LFO (see FMLFO) modulates
    this channel's amplitude and pitch.

FMLFO.doc:
Global LFO on/off and rate (register 0x22). Shared by all 6 channels.

    A channel only hears it if its FMPan sets ams/pms above zero — that
    split (one global rate, per-channel depth) is the chip's, not ours.

FMVolume.doc:
Channel volume 0-127 (127 = loudest), applied to the patch's carriers.

    Attenuating a modulator would change the timbre, not the level, so this
    walks the algorithm's carrier set and adds attenuation only there.

FMPitch.doc:
Detune the channel by `cents` (+/-, 100 = a semitone).

    Applies to the currently sounding note immediately and to later notes
    on the channel until changed — vibrato, pitch envelopes and slides are
    a series of these.

DACEnable.doc: Switch FM channel 6 between normal FM and the 8-bit PCM DAC (register 0x2B).

DACSample.doc:
Play a PCM sample through the DAC. `name` indexes samples.KIT.

    This is the Genesis drum trick: FM channel 6 gives up its voice and
    becomes an 8-bit sample player, which is how Streets of Rage and
    Contra: Hard Corps get real drums out of the chip.

PSGVolume.doc:
Set a PSG channel's attenuation without retriggering its note.

    Channel 3 is the noise voice. PSG has no envelope generator at all, so
    a volume ramp — every PSG decay you have ever heard — is literally a
    run of these events.

cells.dac: clap, hat, hat_open, kick, rim, snare, tom | ...

tracker_syntax.comments: ; anywhere, or # at line start / after whitespace

example:
title chipgen example
bpm 150
lpb 4
inst fm0 bass
inst fm1 square_lead
inst fm2 strings
pan fm2 C 0 2
cols fm0 fm1 fm2 psg0 noise dac

D-2  ...  D-4  D-5   ...  kick
...  ...  ...  A-5:6 ...  hat
A-2  A-4  ...  F-5   w1   snare
...  ...  ...  A-5:6 ...  hat
A#2  ...  A#3  D-5   ...  kick
...  C-5  ...  A-5:6 ...  hat
F-2  ...  ...  C-5   w1   snare
...  A-4  ===  ===   ===  hat
